title: August and the Echo
premise: Freya Yarrow, the last xenolinguist on a failing colony world, has spent years recording dying languages—including her own, which she no longer dreams in. When a ghost ship's manifest surfaces bearing a name that shouldn't exist—her own, dated before she was born—she realizes Earth's forgotten colony was never forgotten at all, but deliberately erased. Racing to the relay at the edge of dead space ahead of Earth's final transmission loop, Freya must choose between broadcasting the truth of the colony's abandonment and preserving the fragile loyalty of the survivors who kept her alive. In the end, she sends both: the truth and an echo of every recorded voice, letting the dead colony speak for itself as the loop closes forever.
about_author: Elodie Whitlock is a former field linguist who spent a decade documenting endangered languages across three continents before turning to science fiction. She writes from a converted radio station on the northern coast, where she still keeps one antenna pointed at the sky.

chapters.title: The Manifest of Ships That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Freya Yarrow, cataloguing the colony's dying archives, discovers a ship manifest listing a passenger named Freya Yarrow—born forty years before her own birth. Her POV establishes isolation and quiet dread as she cross-references records that keep rewriting themselves. The emotional beat is uncanny recognition: the colony's erasure has a face, and it might be hers.

chapters.title: What the Survivors Kept
chapters.summary: Freya confronts the colony council, led by her mentor Oskar, who admits the founders bargained with Earth: silence about the failed terraforming in exchange for supplies that stopped coming anyway. Told from Freya's POV with flashbacks in Oskar's voice, this chapter explores loyalty vs. truth—the community that saved her also buried itself. The beat is betrayal wrapped in love.

chapters.title: Dead Space, Live Signal
chapters.summary: Freya steals the last working skiff and races toward the edge-of-dead-space relay as Earth's transmission loop nears its end. Pursued by Oskar's loyalists who fear exposure will doom them all, she deciphers the manifest's true origin: the first Freya Yarrow was the colony's original negotiator, erased for refusing the bargain. The climax hits at the relay—she must broadcast or stay silent.

chapters.title: An Echo Is Not a Lie
chapters.summary: At the relay, Freya transmits everything: the betrayal, the survival, and years of recorded voices in languages no one dreams in anymore. Oskar arrives too late to stop her—and chooses, finally, to add his own confession to the signal. The resolution lands on inheritance: the colony dies, but its echo outlives the loop, and Freya begins dreaming again—in every language but her own.
